meta.sparkline: 10 points per bout and side, index-only (BFO's chart uses pointStart 1, no time axis): point 0 = the opener (one book's first price, multiplicative de-vig), points 1-8 = BFO mean odds in between, point 9 = mean of the books' closing odds (power de-vig of mean decimal odds, research/model_market.md)
meta.protocol: rows dated >= 2026-01-01 dropped at parse; every choice by forward-chained CV <= 2023 (stack gate 2021-2023, fit 2019..Y-1, tools/ml2.py's 0.0005 rule); 2024-2025 scored once per pre-registration (prereg, prereg_addendum); 2,000 card-cluster bootstrap resamples, paired; no intercepts, corner swap asserted
meta.orientation: A = the first ufcstats name; p = P(A wins)

why: Training on a consensus snapshot passed the pre-2024 gate (consensus minus open-trained, both fed points 4-9: -0.0012 [-0.0033, +0.0009]; against fwd-4.1 as run: -0.0015 [-0.0035, +0.0005]) but the pre-registered 2024-2025 primary was contradicted: +0.0041 [+0.0017, +0.0066]; as run +0.0028 [-0.0001, +0.0059]. Under PREREG's failure rule the open-trained stack stays primary for consensus lines, and under docs/V6_V10_PLAN.md 6.3 the change also fails 'not worse' (CI upper > +0.002)

Among consensus snapshots the training point barely matters (cross-feed spread <= 0.0005 in CV; T-6h..T-7d synthetic lines give the same weights within 0.02). The stacks differ mainly in the ML v2 weight (open-trained 0.58, consensus 0.39, close-trained 0.33), and 2024-2025 rewards ML v2 weight whatever line is fed (open-trained beats close-trained even on the close there). That is a drift / calibration question for the calib workstream, not a line-timing one
routing.not_actionable: on 2024-2025 the open-trained stack fed the POWER de-vig beat it fed the multiplicative de-vig, +0.0014 [+0.0001, +0.0025] for multiplicative; CV says tie (+0.0003), so nothing changes (selection on 2024-2025 is not allowed); a candidate secondary column for the forward ledger
